name: Wilder Kaiser & Kaiserbachtal
kurzbeschreibung: The majestic Kaisergebirge, a paradise for mountaineers and hikers, boasts breathtaking peaks and untouched scenery.
preis: Kostenlos (Mautstraße Kaiserbachtal ca. 4–5 € pro PKW; Parkplatz Wochenbrunner Alm ca. 5 €)
beschreibung:
Overview

The Wilder Kaiser ranks among the most sculpted, dramatic, and storied limestone massifs in the Northern Limestone Alps. With its pale vertical battlements, jagged towers, and cavernous cirques, the range rises dominantly above the Tyrolean towns of Ellmau, Going, Scheffau, and Kufstein, crowned by its highest summit, the Ellmauer Halt (2,344 m). Protected as a pristine nature sanctuary since 1963, the Kaisergebirge encompasses over 92 square kilometers of strictly preserved alpine wilderness. Within mountaineering lore, the Wilder Kaiser commands near-mythic reverence: legendary pioneers such as Hermann Buhl, Hans Dülfer, and Peter Aschenbrenner established benchmark ascents along the sheer faces of the Fleischbank, Totenkirchl, and Predigtstuhl that revolutionized modern rock climbing. Beyond high-stakes alpinism, the range provides accessible scenic wonderlands for hikers, families, and leisurely walkers, notably within the romantic Kaiserbachtal valley and around crystal-clear Lake Hintersteiner See.

Route & Requirements

Hikes across the Wilder Kaiser range from tranquil valley rambles to demanding via ferratas and exposed ridge traverses. The signature family outing explores the verdant Kaiserbachtal from Griesenau to the Griesner Alm (1,024 m): a broad, car-free riverside trail wanders gently upstream beneath the colossal north faces of the Fleischbank and Predigtstuhl (approx. 1 hour, easy grade T1, fully stroller accessible). Active mountain walkers favor the classic ascent from Wochenbrunner Alm up to the Gruttenhütte (1,620 m)—the highest alpine refuge in the range: traversing a scenic, gravel-strewn trail, the route climbs 540 vertical meters in roughly 1.5 to 2 hours (moderate grade T2, requiring surefootedness on rocky switchbacks). Scaling the Ellmauer Halt summit or crossing the Jubiläumssteig demands mountaineering expertise, total head for heights, and helmet/harness gear (T4/C). Sturdy hiking boots are essential. Leashed dogs are welcome on all standard hiking trails.

Visit & Arrival

Rail passengers travel comfortably via ÖBB or Bavarian regional trains to Kufstein, Wörgl, or St. Johann in Tirol, connecting directly to regional VVT buses servicing Ellmau, Scheffau, Going, and Griesenau. Across the summer season, the complimentary "KaiserJet" shuttle bus links villages, trailheads, swimming lakes, and cable cars seamlessly. Motorists arrive toll-free from Bavaria via Kufstein or take the Inntal autobahn A12 (exit Kufstein-Süd or Wörgl-Ost) along federal highway B178. Paid trail parking is located at Wochenbrunner Alm and the Kaiserbachtal entrance.

Tips

Witness the evening alpenglow from the sun terrace of the Gruttenhütte, when the sheer limestone needles of the Kaiser crown illuminate in blazing crimson hues. Sport climbers and spectators should visit the Schleier Waterfall near Going—an open-air arena celebrated worldwide as one of Europe's premier extreme sport climbing crags.
saison: Mai bis Oktober (Winterwandern im Tal möglich)
